taxonomyNote: NatureServe spells the common name Diamond-backed Terrapin and says subspecies are poorly defined and possibly clinal.
fieldMarks: Keeled grey-to-black carapace with deep concentric growth rings; plastron unhinged, yellowish to greenish with dark flecks.
Grey head and neck with conspicuous black spots; consistently white upper lip.
Carapace 10-14 cm in males, 15-24 cm in females.
Unlike snapping turtles it lacks a long saw-toothed tail; unlike mud turtles it has no hinged plastron; unlike wood turtle no orange on neck and limbs.
behavior: Wary and quick to flee; basks on oyster beds and mudflats.
Burrows into mud when inactive; may hibernate in moist sand; ventures into grassy lowlands at high tide.
Eats marine clams, snails, worms and crabs, and scavenges.
habitat: Coastal marshes, tidal flats, coves, estuaries and lagoons behind barrier beaches; brackish water, intolerant of long-term fresh or full-strength salt water.
range: Atlantic and Gulf coasts from Cape Cod to Texas.
